## 2. Lint rules

Declared as data in `lint_cache_docs.py`; `--selftest` asserts each one fires.

| Rule | Scope | Checks |
|------|-------|--------|
| `RC001` | code | Shard/replica index must not be derived from a hash of the key (deterministic selection spreads nothing). |
| `RC002` | code | Single-value type assertion on an interface returned by cache/singleflight (panics on an unexpected type; use the two-value form). |
| `RC003` | code | Sentinel error compared with == instead of errors.Is (a wrapped error silently makes it false). |
| `RC004` | code | Redis write whose error is discarded in a non-anti-example (a silent populate/invalidate failure is invisible and unbounded). |
| `RC005` | code | rand.Intn/Int31n/Int63n whose argument can be zero (panics). |
| `RC006` | prose | Write-through must not be sold as strong/zero-staleness without the cache-write failure semantics that bound it. |
| `RC007` | skill | Value-shape guidance must name the listpack thresholds and gate per-field TTL on HEXPIRE/7.4 -- and each claim must live in its OWN bullet. |
| `RC008` | global | Distributed-lock guidance must cover fencing, bounded renewal and failover -- TTL + token + CAS alone is not a safe lock. |
| `RC009` | skill | Gate 1 blocking items must appear in a STOP condition and must not be described as assumable. |
| `RC010` | skill | Scorecard tier counts in the verdict line must equal the number of checkboxes actually listed in each tier. |
| `RC013` | code | Blocking O(N) or destructive command on a live keyspace (KEYS/FLUSHALL/FLUSHDB) -- single-threaded Redis stalls every other client meanwhile. |
| `RC012` | code | Cache write with an explicit zero expiration (no TTL) -- the entry never expires, so a missed invalidation is stale forever, not stale until TTL. |
| `RC011` | global | Prose must not recommend hash-of-key shard/replica notation without repudiating it (RC001 only sees code blocks). |

## 3. Golden fixtures

`detectors` are the rules that MUST fire on the snippet — asserted in both
directions, so an over-broad rule fails too. `gated by` names the rule that
catches the *headline* defect; `—` means only a model review can, which is
recorded per fixture rather than left silent.

| ID | Title | Type | Severity | Detectors | Gated by |
|----|-------|------|----------|-----------|----------|
| CACHE-001 | No consistency strategy — DB and cache both written without invalidation logic | defect | critical | `RC004`, `RC012` | — |
| CACHE-002 | No TTL on hot cached data — immortal keys with no expiration | defect | critical | `RC004`, `RC012` | `RC012` |
| CACHE-003 | No cache-down degradation — Redis failure causes service 500 | defect | critical | — | — |
| CACHE-004 | Cache-aside without stampede protection — hot key miss causes DB overload | defect | standard | `RC003`, `RC004` | — |
| CACHE-005 | Distributed lock without TTL or safe release — deadlock risk | defect | standard | `RC004`, `RC012` | `RC012` |
| CACHE-006 | KEYS command for batch invalidation — blocks Redis for entire scan | defect | standard | `RC004`, `RC013` | `RC013` |
| CACHE-007 | Well-formed cache-aside with singleflight + TTL jitter + null caching | good_practice | none | — | — |
| CACHE-008 | Good write-through with bounded staleness on cache-write failure | good_practice | none | — | — |
| CACHE-009 | Degraded mode — cache review with no Redis config or consistency requirement | degradation_scenario | none | `RC004` | — |
| CACHE-010 | Workflow — design cache layer from scratch for e-commerce product catalog | workflow | none | — | — |
| CACHE-011 | Cache penetration — non-existent IDs bypass cache and always hit DB | defect | standard | `RC003`, `RC004` | — |
| CACHE-012 | Write-behind for financial transactions — async DB write risks silent data loss | defect | critical | `RC004` | — |
| CACHE-013 | Redis L2 cache without L1 — no avalanche protection when Redis goes down | defect | standard | `RC003`, `RC004` | — |
| CACHE-014 | Multi-tenant shared cache without tenant prefix — cross-tenant data leak | defect | critical | `RC003`, `RC004` | — |
| CACHE-015 | Redis outage masked as a cache miss — degradation policy silently bypassed | defect | critical | `RC004`, `RC012` | — |
| CACHE-016 | Read-populate races write-invalidate — cache-aside restores a stale value permanently | defect | critical | `RC004`, `RC012` | — |
| CACHE-017 | Lock TTL expires mid-work — well-formed lock, no fencing, duplicated external effect | defect | critical | — | — |

**3/13** defect fixtures have their headline defect
mechanically gated. The rest depend on the model reading SKILL.md — that is
